text:
Kyle: Thanks for the great AH discussion. A few follow-ups about hiring approvals, reforecast cadence, and how we treat big equipment purchases (capex vs opex). Post any specific questions here and we'll answer.

Priya: Quick one 1: if I open a req before headcount approval, is that allowed? Our recruiters sometimes need to engage candidates early.

Lena: You can source candidates proactively, but an active req (and offer) requires approved headcount. Tag the req with 'predraft' in Lever and include hiring partner + expected budget owner.

Dev: Suppose we have an urgent IC hire we want to accelerate this quarter - is there a fast-track approval path?

Kyle: For mission-critical roles, manager + director can request an expedited approval from finance. We review runway impact and risk. Typical turnaround 48h, add rationale and expected start date.

Mike: Reforecast note: we run a rolling reforecast each month. If hires shift between quarters we need to update the headcount model by the 5th business day so FP&A can reflect it in cash planning.

Priya: Who signs off on reforecasted hiring slippage? Recruiting or Finance?

Mike: Both. Recruiting provides timing, Finance updates impact to burn. Final sign-off is the budget owner + FP&A.

Dev: Capex vs opex: we have a vendor offering long-term leased on-prem infra. How to classify and who signs?

Jordan: Classification depends on contract terms (ownership transfer, useful life, and capital thresholds). Legal + Finance must review any lease/purchase > $50k. Use the procurement pre-check to flag potential capex.

Beth: Operationally, include expected useful life and payment schedule in your procurement request. If capex treatment is likely, procurement will attach CAPEX approval and liaise with accounting.

Dev: And funding? Do we charge capex to the same cost center?

Mike: We allocate capex to the requesting business unit but also track it on the balance sheet. For multi-team assets, provide allocation percentages.

Priya: How do signing authority limits work for hiring contractors vs full-time offers?

Lena: Offer approvals follow the approval matrix: managers approve up to IC2, directors up to IC4, execs for higher. Contractors follow a separate spend approval: contracting up to $25k can be approved by manager+finance; above that needs procurement + legal.

Dev: What about reimbursements/travel and dev conference budget? Any freeze?

Beth: No freeze on required travel. Team conference budgets are being prioritized: talk to your manager about required attendance. Expense reports should be submitted within 30 days; late claims may be delayed in processing.

Kyle: We're targeting 12+ months runway, so approvals will be more scrutinized for discretionary programs. That doesn't mean no hiring, but more focus on ROI and criticality.

Priya: If a candidate negotiates sign-on or relocation that pushes offer over the cap, who handles approval?

Lena: Escalate to People Ops + Finance. Small relocations (< $5k) can be approved at manager level; larger packages require sign-off from People Ops director and Finance.

Jordan: Reminder: any contractual compensation addendum must be reviewed by Legal before sending the final offer.

Invoices Bot: Heads-up: capital invoices and vendor invoices with 'capex' in the description must include the PO and asset metadata. Missing fields -> routed to finance hold.

Mike: We'll publish a short decision tree and the headcount calendar after the reforecast closes next Tuesday. Office hours for hiring questions will be open Wed/Thu.

Dev: Appreciate it, this clears up a lot.

Kyle: Thanks all 1. We'll follow up with the decision tree and the capex checklist in #all-hands pinned.
